text:
sam: Heads-up: CI microbench on PR #12001 shows a ~12% throughput regression for batcher_throughput vs golden. CI blocked the merge.
bench-bot: [CI] microbench/pr-12001 — batcher_throughput: 88.6k toks/s (golden: 101.1k toks/s) delta: -12.4% | tail_latency: 18.9ms (+9.1ms) | link: https://ci.internal/reports/12001

maria: I can triage. Quick question — this landed two changes: lin's kernel-autoselect tweak and grace's kv-warmup prefetch change, right?
aj: Correct. Both merged in the last batch.
lin: Kernel-autoselect only adjusted the cost-threshold heuristic for fp16 kernels (lowered by ~8%). It shouldn't move batching semantics, but it can change chosen kernel for some seqlen distributions.
grace: My change bumped prefetch_count from 8 -> 12 to reduce cold-start tail latencies. Thought it was safe.

maria: Starting a local bisect to isolate. Commands:
```
git checkout main
git bisect start bad_commit good_commit
# run microbench harness: python dev/bench.py --suite=batcher_throughput --repeat 3
git bisect run ./scripts/ci_bench_runner.sh
```

maria: Bisect progress: narrowed to 2 commits; final suspect: 0f3e7c9 (grace) — kv prefetch change. Repro locally: throughput drops similarly.

grace: Huh. I expected prefetch to help. Maybe prefetch is thrashing KV cache and causing more evictions under our CI seqlen sampler.
aj: Can we get a flamegraph or GPU profile on the bad commit? Need to see whether time is spent in memcpy / fallback kernels or just more decode loops.
lin: Running a quick nvprof + sampling on CI replica now. Sample command I used: `python infra/bench_profile.py --target pr-12001 --warmup 200 --steps 400`

maria: Profile snippet (top stacks, bad vs good):
```
BAD (0f3e7c9):
  38% memcpyHtD
  22% kernel: aten_attention_unfused (fallback path)
  15% kv_cache_evict
  10% cuda_sync
GOOD: (before 0f3e7c9)
  12% memcpyHtD
  45% kernel: optimized_qkv
  8% kv_cache_access
```

maria: Looks like increased memcpy and evictions — KV warmup is causing more cache churn, leading to fallback kernels and more host->device copies. Explains throughput and latency hit.

lin: That makes sense: more prefetch threads pushed more entries into the cache leading to eviction of still-warm entries when batcher affinity changes seqlen distribution. We underestimated the working set.

grace: I'll revert the prefetch_count bump in a follow-up PR and add bounds + a seqlen-aware guard. Pushing patch now.

lin: Also proposing a quick kernel-autoselect guard: if the kernel selector would switch to fallback kernel and the batch size/seqlen combo is in a known sweet spot, prefer the older optimized_qkv until we have better cost models. I'll open PR for the guard.

bench-bot: [CI] pr-12003 (revert-kv-prefetch) — microbench batcher_throughput: 99.3k toks/s (delta vs golden: -1.8%) — within threshold. Link: https://ci.internal/reports/12003
ci-bot: Rolling revert landed to unblock rollout.

sam: Nice work — queued the revert. Two follow-ups: (1) add a regression test that simulates our CI seqlen sampler to catch cache-thrashing prefetch changes, (2) add a perf unit that asserts kernel selection stability for hot batch/seqlen combos.

grace: Will add the regression test today, and include telemetry counters for kv_eviction_rate in the bench harness.
maria: I'll add the kernel-selection stability test to the perf-suite.

sam: Thanks all. Quick postmortem notes: cause = aggressive KV prefetch increased working set -> evictions -> more memcpy and fallback kernels -> throughput regression. Fixes: revert + guarded prefetch + kernel-select stability test + metrics.

aj: Filing a short incident note and tagging release-qa.
lin: :thumbsup:
grace: :raised_hands:
